artifact.summary: Implements the permutation operator P_sigma|j> = |sigma(j)> for a chosen sigma in S_4 on one ququart encoded as two qubits (j = 2*spatial + polarization). It is built only from X, CX and the identity, via a decomposition of sigma into basis-state transpositions; each transposition is realised with CX/X gates. The circuit contains no state preparation or measurement. The paper's input state, measurement and linear-optical implementation are out of scope.
register_layout: ququart basis label j = 2*s + p, so |j> = |q1 q0> in Qiskit little-endian ordering

equation_mapping.explanation: P_sigma|j> = |sigma(j)> is built as a sequence of basis-state transpositions, each implemented with X and CX gates.
sgn(sigma) = det P_sigma is a standard group-theory fact. It is not a circuit element, and the circuit does not compute or output parity.
The illustrative Fourier-type input state is input preparation. It is left to the runner, and the circuit does not prepare it.
The single-query distinguishability criterion involves an unspecified measurement observable M. No measurement is included and no parity-testing scheme is reconstructed.

specification_changes.change: The scope is narrowed to the permutation oracle P_sigma alone, acting on a 2-qubit ququart. The permutation is a runtime parameter of the instance.
specification_changes.reason: The abstract gives no explicit parity-determining circuit, input state, or measurement, so only the well-defined permutation operation can be implemented faithfully.

specification_changes.change: The input state, the measurement and the parity read-out are excluded from the circuit.
specification_changes.reason: The task requires an operation without state preparation or measurement. The paper's actual input state and measurement basis are unknown.

specification_changes.change: The determinant/parity relation is treated as background only and is not computed in the circuit.
specification_changes.reason: Parity is a classical property of sigma. No unitary circuit element is specified for it.

assumptions: The ququart is encoded as two qubits with j = 2*spatial + polarization, so qubit 0 is polarization and qubit 1 is spatial.
The permutation sigma is given as a list with sigma[j] being the image of j, and P_sigma|j> = |sigma(j)>.
The ancilla-free construction uses only X and CX gates; global phases are trivial.
unresolved_issues: The paper's actual input state, measurement basis and any ancillary degrees of freedom are not reconstructed.
The linear-optical implementation of the permutations is not modeled.
The circuit does not itself perform the one-step parity determination, because the abstract gives no explicit construction.

validation.detail: Circuit built and transpiled successfully; no independent correctness reference selected.
